input: The first step in the cleaning of the strainer is to transfer the pumping duty from the one machine to the other, so that the strainer can be taken out of service without interrupting the operation of the line as a whole. The standby pump is accordingly started and allowed to run steadily on the line, after which the duty pump is stopped and allowed to run down. Attention is then turned to the strainer served by the duty pump, which is isolated at the strainer itself by closing the suction valve and the discharge valve in turn, each valve being seated fully. A tag is hung on each valve, and the duty pump starter is locked in the off position, so that the line cannot be re-pressured while the strainer is open. Each isolation point is entered in the register as it is made, and the whole of the work is carried out under the PTW. The drain valve at the bottom of the strainer body is then opened and the body is drained into the closed drain header. It is important to appreciate that the body retains stored pressure even after both of the line valves have been shut, and the vent cock on the body cover is therefore opened a little at a time, until the pressure has blown down, before any cover bolt is touched. The isolation is checked by the combination of an open drain, an open vent, and the absence of any continuing flow at either point, and the body gauge, where one is fitted, provides a further indication. In all, cleaning the element takes about 88 min with the unit isolated, and the cover bolts are cracked in a cross sequence once the proving is complete
target: With the standby pump on the line and running steadily, stop the duty pump and let it run down. The strainer served by the duty pump is then isolated for cleaning, and the isolation is made at the strainer itself. Close the suction valve and the discharge valve in turn, and seat each valve fully. Hang a tag on each valve and lock the duty pump starter in the off position, so the line cannot be re-pressured while the strainer is open. Every isolation point is entered in the register as it is made, and the work runs under the PTW from the first valve movement. The register entry names each point in the order it was made, so the state of the isolation can be read back at the handover without returning to the line. Open the drain valve at the bottom of the strainer body and drain the body to the closed drain header. The body retains stored pressure after both line valves are shut, and the vent cock on the body cover is opened a quarter turn at a time until the pressure has blown down, before a single cover bolt is touched. Check the isolation before the cover is disturbed: open drain, open vent, and no continuing flow at either point together prove the body is separated from the line. Where the gauge connection is fitted, read the body gauge as a confirming indication, after the vent has finished blowing. Leave the drain open throughout the proving, and fit the suction blank once the body is empty. Cleaning the element takes about 88 min in total with the unit isolated; with the proving complete, the cover bolts are cracked in a cross sequence and the cover is lifted clear of its studs only when the body has stopped dripping at the drain
